title: How do shadow roots and slots interact with the content model?

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
Because div elements fall into the flow content category and because custom elements are transparent and span elements don't allow flow content as children, the following structure violates the content model:

```
span
└─custom-element
  └─div
```

The following, however, is acceptable:

```
div
└─custom-element
  └─div
```

Although the exact rules are unclear from the specification, most people would probably expect that a custom element that has a shadow root with the following content would also be acceptable:

```
div
└─custom-element
  ├─#shadow-root
  │ └─span
  └─div
```

But what if a custom element has a shadow root containing a slot element? It is unclear how shadow roots and slots interact with the content model. Is the following still acceptable or does it violate the content model because the slot named `foo`, which is transparent and is a child of a span element, will be assigned a div?

```
div
└─custom-element
  ├─#shadow-root
  │ └─span
  │   └─slot name="foo"
  └─div slot="foo"
```

Clarification would be much appreciated.
